extracted.intended_audience: State air pollution control agencies; owners/operators of affected electric generating units (EGUs); EPA Regional Administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and criteria that State plans must include to implement the EPA Carbon Pollution Standards for affected EGUs, including data inventories, standards of performance, enforceable increments of progress, reporting/website obligations, and mechanisms for extensions or reliability exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategory definitions and applicability (load- and fuel-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines subcategories for affected EGUs by fuel type and capacity factor: base load, intermediate load, and low load for oil-fired and natural gas-fired steam generating units (e.g., base load = annual capacity factor >=45%; intermediate = >=8% and <45%; low load <8%), and other subcategories (long-term and medium-term coal-fired steam generating units, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans must identify affected EGUs' subcategory applicability and include enforceable requirements necessary to establish that applicability (see requirements related to subcategory applicability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory of Data from Affected EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include an inventory of specified data for each affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required data include: (i) nameplate capacity (per §60.5880b); (ii) base load rating (per §60.5880b); (iii) continuous 5-year period immediately prior to May 9, 2024 data including (A) sum of CO2 emissions during each quarter, (B) for most subcategories sum of gross energy output each quarter (or for low load natural gas/oil-fired units, sum of heat input each quarter), (C) heat input for each fuel type combusted each quarter, (D) start/end dates of most representative continuous 8-quarter baseline period and sums of CO2 emissions, gross energy output or heat input (as applicable), and heat input by fuel for that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of Performance inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: For each affected EGU the State plan must include the standard of performance that applies to that unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards may be rate-based per §60.5775b(c)-(d) or an alternate form for certain subcategories per §60.5775b(e). Standards must not exceed levels calculated by the methods described in §60.5775b(b) unless established under §60.5775b(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics required for each standard of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of performance in the State plan must be demonstrated to be quantifiable, verifiable, non-duplicative, permanent, and enforceable for each affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifiable = reliably measurable and replicable; Verifiable = adequate monitoring, recordkeeping, reporting to enable independent verification; Non-duplicative = not already incorporated as a standard in the State plan; Permanent = must be met continuously unless replaced by approved State plan revision; Enforceable = technically accurate limitation/time period specified; compliance requirements clearly defined; EGUs responsible and liable for violations; each compliance measure enforceable as practical matter (per 40 CFR 49.167); Administrator/State/third parties retain enforcement ability (cited authorities include CAA sections 113(a)-(h) and 304).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements related to subcategory applicability — permanent cessation for medium-term coal
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must include an enforceable requirement that medium-term coal-fired steam generating units permanently cease operations by a date after December 31, 2031 and before January 1, 2039.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an enforceable applicability requirement establishing the unit's subcategory status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements related to subcategory applicability — removal of coal capability for NG/oil units
rubrics_metrics.description: For steam generating units defined as natural gas- or oil-fired that retain the capability to fire coal after May 9, 2024, fired any coal during the 5-year period prior to that date, or will fire any coal after that date and before January 1, 2030, State plans must include a requirement to remove the capability to fire coal before January 1, 2030.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an enforceable requirement to determine the unit's subcategory applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements related to subcategory applicability — fuel usage estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include, for each affected EGU, an estimate of coal, oil, and natural gas usage by heat input for the first 3 calendar years after January 1, 2030.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides projection information to support subcategory designation and compliance planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements related to subcategory applicability — permanent cessation compliance duties
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs that plan to permanently cease operation, State plans must require compliance with applicable State and Federal requirements for permanently ceasing operations including removal from State air emissions inventories and amending or revoking permits to reflect permanent shutdown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure administrative and permitting actions reflect permanent cessation status; include any necessary enforcement language in State plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increments of Progress — general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include legally enforceable increments of progress for affected EGUs in the long-term coal-fired and medium-term coal-fired subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increments must have calendar-date deadlines and the owner/operator must meet website reporting obligations; increments differ by subcategory and by control strategy (e.g., CCS vs. natural gas co-firing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final control plan content (increment A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submittal of a final control plan for the affected EGU to the air pollution control agency, consistent with the subcategory declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term coal units: final control plan must include supporting analysis including a feasibility and/or FEED study. Medium-term coal units: final control plan must include supporting analysis including design basis for facility modifications, anticipated timeline to achieve full compliance, and anticipated benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarding of contracts (increment B) as demonstration of progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion of awarding of contracts: owners/operators may demonstrate compliance with this increment by submitting sufficient evidence that appropriate contracts have been awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term coal: awarding contracts for emission control systems or process modifications or issuing orders for component parts. Medium-term coal: awarding contracts for boiler modifications or issuing orders for component parts necessary for boiler modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of on-site construction or installation (increment C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiation of on-site construction or installation of emission control equipment or process change required to meet the standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term coal: initiation of on-site construction/installation required to achieve 90% carbon capture annually. Medium-term coal: initiation of on-site construction/installation necessary to enable 40% natural gas co-firing on an annual average basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of on-site construction or installation (increment D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion of on-site construction or installation of emission control equipment or process change required to meet the standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term coal: completion required to achieve 90% carbon capture annually. Medium-term coal: completion of boiler modifications necessary to enable 40% natural gas co-firing on an annual average basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement of permitting actions related to pipeline construction (increment E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must demonstrate commencement of pipeline-related permitting actions by a date specified in the State plan, with supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence must include pipeline planning/design documentation, complete list of pipeline-related permit applications with authorities, attestation that list is complete for authorizations required to operate at full compliance, and a timeline to complete all pipeline permitting activities. Applies to long-term coal units adopting CCS and medium-term units adopting natural gas co-firing where pipeline infrastructure is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report identifying CO2 injection and transport (increment F)
rubrics_metrics.description: For long-term coal units adopting CCS, a report identifying geographic CO2 injection location, CO2 transport from capture to storage, regulatory requirements for sequestration activities, and anticipated permitting timeline must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This increment documents sequestration site and regulatory pathway and timeline for CCS deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incremental compliance dates (increment G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the standard of performance is required by specified dates for subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medium-term coal-fired subcategory: compliance by January 1, 2030. Long-term coal-fired subcategory: compliance by January 1, 2032.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative increments for non-CCS/non-co-firing controls
rubrics_metrics.description: If an affected unit in the long-term coal subcategory will meet its standard using a control other than CCS (or medium-term using a control other than natural gas co-firing), State plans must include appropriate increments of progress consistent with 40 CFR 60.21a(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the increments consistent with the referenced regulation; earliest calendar date must be assigned to the increment corresponding to 40 CFR 60.21a(h)(1); increments corresponding to 60.21a(h)(5) must be assigned specific no-later-than dates (2032 for long-term, 2030 for medium-term).

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting of increments and documentation to Carbon Pollution Standards website
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must post within 30 business days of State plan submittal a description of activities/actions constituting the increments of progress and the schedule, and must post documentation demonstrating each increment has been met within 30 business days of each occurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting is on the Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs website required by §60.5740b(a)(10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to report and post deviations from increments of progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must report to the State regulatory agency any deviation from any federally enforceable increment of progress within 30 business days after knowing or should have known of the event, explaining causes and measures to cure and prevent future deviations, including timeframes; must also post a report of the deviation to the Carbon Pollution Standards website within 30 business days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must describe causes and corrective measures with timeframes; posting ensures public transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting obligations and milestones for EGUs planning permanent cessation — Initial Milestone Report
rubrics_metrics.description: Five years before permanent cessation (or 60 days after State plan submission, whichever is later) owner/operator must submit an Initial Milestone Report containing specified items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must include (A) summary of process steps required to permanently cease operations with timing/duration and notifications; (B) list of key milestones with calendar deadlines including notice to reliability authority and official retirement filing; (C) analysis comparing timelines to similar EGUs that ceased operation within prior 10 years; (D) supporting regulatory documents including correspondence/filings with RTO/ISO/Balancing Authority/PUC, deactivation-related reliability assessments, and SEC filings or investor notices (10-K/10-Q references, integrated resource plans/PUC orders, reliability analyses, notifications altering timing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Milestone Status Report (pre-cessation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each remaining year prior to committed cessation date, owner/operator must submit an annual Milestone Status Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must include (A) progress toward meeting milestones in Initial Milestone Report and (B) supporting regulatory documents and relevant SEC filings demonstrating compliance/progress (correspondence with RTO/ISO/PUC, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Milestone Status Report (post-cessation)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than six months from the date the affected EGU permanently ceases operations, owner/operator must submit a Final Milestone Status Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must document actions taken subsequent to ceasing operation to ensure cessation is permanent, including regulatory filings and decommissioning plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting and deviation reporting for milestone reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must post Initial, annual, and Final Milestone Status Reports (including schedules and supporting documentation) on the Carbon Pollution Standards website within 30 business days of filing and report any deviation from federally enforceable reporting milestones to the State regulatory agency within 30 business days, including posting deviation reports to the website within 30 business days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures public availability and State notification of milestone progress and deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of applicable monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping (MRR) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include all applicable MRR requirements, including initial and ongoing QA/QC procedures, for each affected EGU consistent with or no less stringent than §60.5860b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MRR must enable the verifiability requirement for standards of performance and be enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: State reporting to EPA about State plan implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must describe the process, contents, and schedule for State reporting to EPA regarding State plan implementation and progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear schedule and content requirements so EPA can track implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific requirements for existing coal-fired steam generating EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must include requirements specifically for existing coal-fired steam generating EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include (i) requirement that existing coal-fired EGUs operate only subject to a standard of performance pursuant to §60.5775b or an exemption under §60.5850b (including any extension via reliability assurance mechanism); (ii) list of existing coal-fired EGUs at time of submission that plan to permanently cease operation before Jan 1, 2032, with calendar cessation dates; (iii) provision that operation past listed date constitutes a violation of the State plan unless an extension was granted under the reliability assurance mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs Website requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must require owners/operators to establish a publicly accessible 'Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs' website and to post relevant documents and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators must post subcategory designations, compliance schedules, emissions data and other information needed to demonstrate compliance (including data relevant to increments of progress, milestones, extension requests and approvals). Data should be in a readily downloadable format. States must establish a website that displays links to these EGU websites for all affected EGUs in the State plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Date Extension mechanism — scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans may include provisions allowing a compliance date extension (no longer than one year and only once) for owners/operators installing add-on controls who cannot meet the compliance date due to circumstances beyond their control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions limited to one year and only available once per affected EGU; optional mechanism must require a demonstration of necessity with specific supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Date Extension — required demonstration of necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension request must demonstrate inability to meet the compliance date due to circumstances beyond owner/operator's control and show that all relevant increments of progress were met and all reasonable steps taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstration must: (A) identify each affected unit seeking extension; (B) describe controls to be installed; (C) describe/prove progress toward installing controls, including (1) contracts entered or explanation why none, and (2) permits obtained or permit application and permitting authority statement on anticipated timeframe; (D) identify circumstances beyond control necessitating delay (vendor/engineering info, permit delays, infrastructure construction delays); (E) propose a compliance date no later than one year after the original date and updated increments of progress dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Date Extension — State approval process and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan must assign the State air pollution control agency responsibility to approve/disapprove extension requests based on whether necessary demonstrations and documentation were provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism must require: submission no later than 6 months prior to applicable compliance date; owner/operator must notify EPA Regional Administrator at time of submission; owner/operator must post application on the Carbon Pollution Standards website when submitted; State determination must be posted and, if approved, website info updated within 30 days of approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-Term Reliability Mechanism — availability and authorized issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans may include a short-term reliability mechanism available only during system emergencies as defined in §60.5880b and must identify the entity/entities authorized to issue system emergencies for the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism limited to documented system emergency periods; authorized entities must be listed in the State plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-Term Reliability Mechanism — alternative emission limitation during emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: During a documented system emergency an impacted affected EGU may comply with an emission limitation corresponding to its baseline emission performance rate (per §60.5775b(d)) in lieu of its otherwise applicable standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plan must include the alternative emission limitation as an enforceable emission limitation applicable only during system emergency periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-Term Reliability Mechanism — documentation of the system emergency and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: An affected EGU relying on the short-term reliability mechanism must provide documentation that the system emergency occurred and that the unit was impacted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation required includes (A) evidence system emergency was in effect and duration from issuing entity; (B) documentation that the emergency included the affected region/source; (C) documentation that the source was instructed to increase output or remain in operation outside scheduled dispatch from Reliability Coordinator/Balancing Authority/ISO/RTO; (D) data collected during event including sum of CO2 emissions, sum of gross energy output, and resulting CO2 emissions performance rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-Term Reliability Mechanism — recordkeeping of emergency operation hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to document the hours an affected EGU operated under a system emergency and which enforceable emission limitation (baseline or otherwise) applied during those hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This documentation supports compliance demonstrations and must be included in records and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-Term Reliability Mechanism — compliance demonstration treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: For demonstrating compliance with the applicable standard of performance, the affected EGU may use its baseline emissions rate (per §60.5775b(d)) in lieu of its otherwise applicable standard for hours operated during the system emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectively exempts emergency hours from the standard and substitutes the baseline rate for compliance calculations for those hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-Term Reliability Mechanism — public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions defining the short-term reliability mechanism must be part of the public comment process during State plan development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency and opportunity for public input on emergency operation allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability Assurance Mechanism — scope and eligible EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans may include a reliability assurance mechanism allowing one extension (not to exceed 12 months) of an affected EGU's planned permanent cessation date if operation is necessary for electric grid reliability; applies only to eligible EGUs defined in the mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible EGUs include (A) coal-fired units exempt under §60.5850b(k); (B) medium-term coal units with enforceable commitments to cease before Jan 1, 2039 included in the State plan; (C) affected EGUs with enforceable cessation dates included in State plan per §60.24a(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability Assurance Mechanism — preconditions for granting extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions only available if owner/operator has satisfied all applicable increments of progress, reporting obligations, and milestones (paragraphs (a)(5) and (6)) and has posted all relevant information on the Carbon Pollution Standards website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures extensions are not granted absent full demonstration of progress and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability Assurance Mechanism — standard of performance remains in place
rubrics_metrics.description: Any applicable standard of performance must remain in place during the duration of an extension under the reliability assurance mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension does not suspend applicable standards; compliance obligations continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability Assurance Mechanism — procedures for short vs longer extensions and review authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions up to 6 months must be submitted to EPA Regional Administrator for review/approval; extensions >6 months up to 12 months must be submitted to FERC (through designated process/office) and to the EPA Regional Administrator for review/approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different review pathways and timetables depending on requested extension length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability Assurance Mechanism — application contents for ≤6 months
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply for an extension ≤6 months, owner/operator must submit a complete written application no less than 30 days prior to cease date (but no earlier than 12 months) including required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must include (A) analysis demonstrating EGU is critical to electric reliability and projection of how long it will be reliability-critical (requested extension ≤ that period and ≤6 months); analysis must show that cease would cause either (1) noncompliance with mandatory FERC reliability standards, or (2) increase in loss of load expectation beyond regional planning targets; (B) certification from relevant reliability planning authority with supporting analysis; (C) copies of any written third-party comments; (D) demonstration plan from owner/operator/grid operator/others of steps/timeframes to resolve underlying reliability issue; (E) any other info requested by EPA Regional Administrator or FERC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability Assurance Mechanism — application contents and timing for >6 to 12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply for an extension >6 months up to 12 months, owner/operator must submit an application with the same information but with a 12-month analysis period; must be submitted to EPA Regional Administrator no less than 45 days prior to listed cease date (but no earlier than 12 months prior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer extension applications involve additional timeliness and submission to FERC as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability Assurance Mechanism — limits and reuse restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions will be granted only for the period substantiated by the reliability need and shall not exceed 12 months in total; the mechanism cannot be used more than once to extend an eligible EGU's planned cessation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA Regional Administrator may reject incomplete or inadequate submissions; overall restrictions prevent repeated use or indefinite extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of standards of performance (rate-based or alternate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of performance for each affected EGU may take the form of: (1) a rate-based standard for an individual EGU that does not exceed levels calculated via methods in §60.5775b(c) and (d); or (2) an alternate form which may apply for affected EGUs in the long-term or medium-term coal-fired subcategories as provided in §60.5775b(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plan must specify which form applies for each EGU and demonstrate compatibility with the methodology in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable standard methodology — long-term coal-fired units
rubrics_metrics.description: For long-term coal-fired steam generating units: the Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER) is CCS with 90% capture of CO2; degree of emission limitation is 88.4% reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross); the presumptively approvable standard is an emission rate limit defined by an 88.4% reduction in annual emission rate from the unit-specific baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans using the presumptively approvable approach for long-term coal units should apply these BSER and degree-of-control figures and calculate unit-specific emission rate limits based on the unit baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable standard methodology — medium-term coal-fired units
rubrics_metrics.description: For medium-term coal-fired steam generating units: the BSER is natural gas co-firing at 40% of heat input; degree of emission limitation is 16% reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross); the presumptively approvable standard is an emission rate limit defined by a 16% reduction in annual emission rate from the unit-specific baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans using the presumptively approvable approach for medium-term coal units should apply these BSER and degree-of-control figures and calculate unit-specific emission rate limits based on the unit baseline.
